plain_english_revision: The amendment replaces the original bill with a new measure that would require parental consent for Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR) orders on minors, unless certain conditions are met. It also introduces a new legal framework called 'Simon's Law' to govern end-of-life care decisions for qualified minors, including detailed procedures for obtaining consent and resolving conflicts between parents or representatives.
candidate_position_supported: Advancing parental involvement in medical decision-making for minors regarding life-sustaining treatments, including DNAR orders, and establishing a structured legal process to resolve conflicts among caregivers.
evidence_quotes: A Do Not Attempt Resuscitation order... shall not be instituted for a qualified minor until both of the following occur: Consent is obtained from the representative of the qualified minor for a DNAR order. A reasonable attempt is made to inform one or the other parent of the consent by the representative of the qualified minor.
No physician, licensed health care professional... shall be subject to criminal or civil liability... in the absence of actual knowledge of the revocation thereof
A representative of a qualified minor, attending physician, or health care facility may petition a circuit court... for an order enjoining a violation or threatened violation of this chapter.
review_reason: The amendment text is clear and comprehensive enough to determine its primary policy effect without ambiguity.
